text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash involve the eyebrows, or do you notice any redness behind the ears or in the diaper area? Has the baby shown any signs of itching or discomfort, such as rubbing his head against the bedding?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Skin_Biopsy
The presence of greasy yellow scales on the scalp and forehead in an infant strongly suggests seborrheic dermatitis, often referred to as "cradle cap." I want to rule out psoriasis given the family history, so I am ordering a skin biopsy for confirmation.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal biopsy results effectively rule out psoriasis and other inflammatory dermatoses, confirming this is benign seborrheic dermatitis. I will now provide you with the typical clinical images of infantile seborrheic dermatitis for your reference. REQUEST IMAGES
